title: How can the numbers one to sixteen be written in a base four system?
description: The board makes its own base four symbols, then writes every number from one to sixteen with them. The last number is checked by regrouping, as in the base five example.
teaching_notes: One idea: in base four, four of any symbol are regrouped into one symbol of the next landmark. Watch for students who write four sticks and leave them as they are.

source: Figure it Out (bases and their limits, question 2)
video_script.why: The child builds a base four system by the same landmark and biggest-first method used in the base five example.
video_script.substitution: Instead of base five with five of a shape regrouped, the base is four and four of a symbol are regrouped.
video_script.anchor: the book's idea of making your own number system, here with base four and three new symbols
video_script.payoff_line: The landmarks are one, four and sixteen.

final_answer.value: Landmarks 1, 4, 16; for example 7 is a stick and 3 dots, 12 is 3 sticks, 16 is one square
final_answer.spoken: the landmarks are one, four and sixteen, and for example seven is a stick and three dots, twelve is three sticks, and sixteen is one square

hold_back: Landmarks 1, 4, 16; for example 7 is a stick and 3 dots, 12 is 3 sticks, 16 is one square
maths_rules: 1, 2, 3 = 1, 2, 3 dots; 4 = a stick; 5, 6, 7 = a stick and 1, 2, 3 dots; 8 = 2 sticks
9, 10, 11 = 2 sticks and 1, 2, 3 dots; 12 = 3 sticks; 13, 14, 15 = 3 sticks and 1, 2, 3 dots
check: 3 sticks and 3 dots = 12 + 3 = 15; no symbol is used 4 or more times
video_script.design: One idea: four of a symbol regroup into the next. The dot, stick and square stay on the board while the numbers are written below them.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the words base 4 and the numbers 1 to 16 in a row; three empty boxes for symbols

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.ask: base 4, the numbers 1 to 16 and three empty boxes appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about making your own number system.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must use base four, and write every number from one to sixteen.
Which landmark numbers will base four have?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board with the three empty boxes

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: five triangles slide into a square in base 5; a bundle of the base number slides into the next landmark

marks.rule: a bundle of the base number of one landmark slides into the next
marks.sym: each landmark gets its own symbol
marks.big: the biggest landmark that fits is taken first

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>In a base system, the first landmark is one. Each next landmark is the base times the one before.
<bookmark mark='sym'/>Each landmark gets its own symbol.
<bookmark mark='big'/>We write a number by taking the biggest landmark that fits first.

marks.given: base 4 and the numbers 1 to 16 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, base four, and the numbers from one to sixteen.

beats.on_screen: To find: landmarks; symbols; each number 1 to 16

marks.find: the three things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the landmarks, choose symbols, and write every number from one to sixteen.

marks.mult: start 1 and the rule times 4 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step one, start at one and multiply by four each time.
<bookmark mark='land'/>One times four is four, and four times four is sixteen. The next landmark would be more than sixteen, so we stop here.
<bookmark mark='dot'/>Step two, give each landmark a symbol. We choose a dot for one.
<bookmark mark='stick'/>We choose a stick for four, and a square for sixteen.
<bookmark mark='square'/>These three symbols are all we need.

beats.on_screen: 1, 2, 3 = 1, 2, 3 dots; 4 = a stick; 5, 6, 7 = a stick and 1, 2, 3 dots; 8 = 2 sticks

marks.dots: one, two and three dots are drawn for 1, 2 and 3
marks.five: a stick with one, two and three dots is drawn for 5, 6 and 7

narration: <bookmark mark='dots'/>Step three, write the numbers from one. One, two and three are one, two and three dots.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four is a stick, because four dots join into one stick.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Five, six and seven are a stick with one, two and three dots.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>Eight is two sticks, which is two groups of four.

beats.on_screen: 9, 10, 11 = 2 sticks and 1, 2, 3 dots; 12 = 3 sticks; 13, 14, 15 = 3 sticks and 1, 2, 3 dots

marks.nine: two sticks with one, two and three dots are drawn for 9, 10 and 11
marks.thirteen: three sticks with one, two and three dots are drawn for 13, 14 and 15

narration: <bookmark mark='nine'/>Step four, carry on. Nine, ten and eleven are two sticks with one, two and three dots.
<bookmark mark='twelve'/>Twelve is three sticks, which is three groups of four.
<bookmark mark='thirteen'/>Thirteen, fourteen and fifteen are three sticks with one, two and three dots.

marks.sixteen: four sticks slide together into one square for 16

narration: <bookmark mark='sixteen'/>Step five, write sixteen. Four sticks would make sixteen, but four sticks join to make the next landmark. Sixteen is one square.

beats.on_screen: check: 3 sticks and 3 dots = 12 + 3 = 15; no symbol is used 4 times

marks.check: 3 sticks and 3 dots is written as 12 + 3 = 15 and ticked
marks.none: the list is ticked: no symbol appears four or more times

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step six, check by adding back. Three sticks and three dots are twelve plus three, which is fifteen.
<bookmark mark='none'/>No symbol is ever used four times, because four would be regrouped.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Landmarks 1, 4, 16; for example 7 is a stick and 3 dots, 12 is 3 sticks, 16 is one square

marks.ex: the examples for 7, 12 and 16 are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The landmarks are one, four and sixteen.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>For example, seven is a stick and three dots. Twelve is three sticks, and sixteen is one square.
